name: Adam
footnote: First human formed from the ground; his name is literally what he was made from.

name: Eve (Chavah)
footnote: Mother of all living; the name God (and Adam) gave her after the promise of redemption.

name: Cain
footnote: Eve said, “I have acquired a man with the help of the LORD” — but he became the first murderer.

name: Abel
footnote: His life was short and “vanished like a breath” — the first martyr.

name: Seth
footnote: “God has appointed another seed instead of Abel” — the chosen line continues through him.

name: Enosh
footnote: In his days “men began to call upon the name of the LORD” — highlights human weakness.

name: Kenan (Cainan)
footnote: Continues the line; name echoes the “acquired” theme of the pre-flood world.

name: Mahalalel
meaning: “Praise of God” / “the shining one of God” (Hebrew mahalal + El)
footnote: His very name is a shout of praise in a darkening world.

name: Jared
footnote: Traditional Jewish interpretation: “he shall come down” — pointing to the descent of the sons of God or the coming judgment.

name: Enoch
footnote: Walked so closely with God he was “taken” without dying — fully dedicated.

name: Methuselah
meaning: “When he dies, it shall be sent” / “man of the dart” (Hebrew muth + shelach)
footnote: His death coincided with the Flood — his name was a 969-year prophecy of judgment.

name: Lamech
footnote: Father of Noah; spoke of relief from the curse — but his line produced violence.

name: Noah
footnote: “This one will bring us relief from our work and the toil of our hands” — the ark brought rest from judgment.

name: Shem
footnote: Ancestor of the Semitic line; through him came the “Name” (the line that would bear God’s name).

name: Japheth
footnote: “May God enlarge Japheth” — his descendants spread across the earth.

name: Ishmael
footnote: God heard Hagar’s affliction in the wilderness.

name: Esau
footnote: Born hairy and red; sold his birthright for red stew.

name: Jacob
footnote: Grabbed Esau’s heel at birth; later supplanted him and became Israel.

name: Israel
footnote: Wrestled with God and prevailed; name of the covenant nation.

name: Reuben
footnote: Leah’s first son; “Behold, a son!” — hoped it would win Jacob’s love.

name: Simeon
footnote: “The LORD has heard that I am hated” — Leah’s second son.

name: Levi
footnote: “Now my husband will be joined to me” — tribe of priests.

name: Judah
footnote: “This time I will praise the LORD” — royal tribe and ancestor of Messiah.

name: Joseph
footnote: God added to his blessings despite betrayal; savior of his family.

name: Benjamin
footnote: Rachel’s last son; “son of my sorrow” became “son of the right hand.”

name: Moses
footnote: Drawn out of the Nile; drew Israel out of Egypt.

name: Aaron
footnote: First high priest; exalted to lead worship.

name: Joshua (Yehoshua)
footnote: Led Israel into the Promised Land; name points to the ultimate Savior.

name: Caleb
footnote: Followed the LORD fully; entered the land.

name: Rahab
footnote: God’s mercy was broad enough to save a Canaanite prostitute.

name: Ruth
footnote: Loyal friend to Naomi; became ancestor of David and Messiah.

name: Samuel
footnote: God heard Hannah’s prayer; last judge and anointer of kings.

name: Saul
footnote: The people “asked for” a king; first king of Israel.

name: David
footnote: The beloved king; “a man after God’s own heart.”

name: Solomon
footnote: Brought peace and built the Temple.

name: Elijah
footnote: Confronted Baal worship; “My God is Yahweh.”

name: Elisha
footnote: Continued Elijah’s work; brought salvation and healing.

name: Isaiah
footnote: Prophesied the coming Savior who would save His people.

name: Jeremiah
footnote: Exalted God even while weeping over Jerusalem.

name: Ezekiel
footnote: Strengthened by God during exile.

name: Daniel
footnote: Stood before earthly kings; God was his true Judge.

name: Hosea
footnote: His life pictured God’s faithful salvation of unfaithful Israel.

name: Jonah
footnote: Symbol of peace; fled yet brought salvation to Nineveh.

name: Micah
footnote: Asked the rhetorical question that points to God’s uniqueness.

name: Nahum
footnote: Brought comfort by announcing the end of Nineveh’s oppression.

name: Habakkuk
footnote: Embraced God in faith despite coming judgment.

name: Zephaniah
footnote: Hidden and protected the remnant during judgment.

name: Haggai
footnote: Urged the people to rebuild the Temple for God’s festivals.

name: Zechariah
footnote: God remembered His covenant promises.

name: Malachi
footnote: The last Old Testament messenger before John the Baptist.

name: Esther (Hadassah)
footnote: Hidden like a star; saved her people.

name: Mordecai
footnote: Humble servant who refused to bow to Haman.

name: Ezra
footnote: Helped restore the Law and the people after exile.

name: Nehemiah
footnote: Comforted and rebuilt Jerusalem’s walls.

name: Mary (Miriam)
footnote: Mother of Jesus; experienced bitterness yet exaltation.

name: Joseph (NT)
footnote: God added protection and provision for the holy family.

name: John (Yochanan)
footnote: Forerunner of Jesus; proclaimed God’s grace.

name: Jesus (Yeshua)
footnote: The ultimate fulfillment: “He will save His people from their sins.”

name: Peter (Cephas / Petros)
footnote: The rock on which the Church would be built.

name: Andrew
footnote: Courageous fisherman turned fisher of men.

name: James (Jacob)
footnote: One of the “sons of thunder”; later a pillar of the Church.

name: Philip
meaning: “Lover of horses” (used for “lover of people”) (Greek Philippos)
footnote: Brought people to Jesus (e.g., the Ethiopian eunuch).

name: Bartholomew (Nathanael)
footnote: Jesus called him “an Israelite in whom is no deceit.”

name: Thomas
footnote: Doubting Thomas; later declared “My Lord and my God!”

name: Matthew (Levi)
footnote: Tax collector given the gift of apostleship and authorship.

name: Simon the Zealot
footnote: Zealous revolutionary transformed into apostle.

name: Judas (not Iscariot)
footnote: Praised God; author of the epistle of Jude.

name: Paul (Saul)
footnote: Changed from “asked for” (Saul) to the humble apostle to the Gentiles.

name: Timothy
footnote: Honored God as Paul’s faithful son in the faith.

name: Titus
footnote: Defended the faith and organized churches.

name: Philemon
footnote: Showed affectionate forgiveness to his runaway slave.

name: Barnabas
footnote: Encouraged the early Church and Paul.

name: Stephen
footnote: Received the martyr’s crown as the first Christian martyr.

name: Lydia
footnote: First European convert; “dealer in purple” (royal trade).

name: Aquila
footnote: Strong “eagle” who with Priscilla taught Apollos.

name: Priscilla
footnote: Venerable teacher alongside her husband.

name: Apollos
footnote: Mighty preacher whose eloquence was refined by Aquila and Priscilla.

name: Silas (Silvanus)
footnote: Steady companion who endured prison with Paul.

name: Onesimus
footnote: The runaway slave who became “useful” to Paul and Philemon.

name: Phoebe
footnote: Radiant deaconess who carried Paul’s letter to Rome.

name: Gaius
footnote: Hospitable host who brought joy to the Church.

name: Erastus
footnote: Beloved city treasurer who served Paul.

name: Demas
footnote: Loved popularity more than Christ and forsook Paul.

name: Mark (John Mark)
footnote: Initially faltered but later became useful to Paul.

name: Luke
footnote: “Beloved physician” who brought gospel light.

name: Theophilus
footnote: The one Luke wrote to — “lover of God.”

name: Diotrephes
footnote: Loved preeminence and opposed apostolic authority.

name: Gamaliel
footnote: Wise teacher who advised the Sanhedrin wisely.

name: Nicodemus
footnote: Came to Jesus by night seeking truth.

name: Lazarus
footnote: Raised from the dead; God helped him.

name: Martha
footnote: Busy homemaker who learned to sit at Jesus’ feet.

name: Mary Magdalene
footnote: “Tower” of strength; first witness to the resurrection.

name: Salome
footnote: Mother of James and John; sought peaceful places at Jesus’ right hand.

name: Barabbas
footnote: Released in place of the true Son of the Father.

name: Pilate (Pontius)
footnote: Roman judge who washed his hands of Jesus.

name: Herod
footnote: Multiple “heroic” kings who opposed God’s plan.

name: Ananias
footnote: Multiple figures shown God’s grace (one healed Paul, one lied).

name: Sapphira
footnote: Beautiful exterior but deceptive heart.

name: Cornelius
footnote: Roman centurion whose “horn” (strength) was turned to God.

name: Felix
footnote: Governor who trembled but never found true happiness.

name: Festus
footnote: Roman governor who heard Paul’s defense joyfully.

name: Agrippa
footnote: King who heard the gospel but remained untamed.

name: Bernice
footnote: Sister of Agrippa; present at Paul’s trial.

name: Artemas
footnote: Faithful coworker Paul sent to Crete.

name: Tychicus
footnote: “Lucky” messenger who carried Paul’s letters.

name: Epaphras
footnote: Lovely intercessor who prayed fervently for Colossae.

name: Archippus
footnote: Called to “fulfill your ministry” like a faithful rider.

name: Apphia
footnote: Hostess whose house church grew.

name: Euodia
footnote: Worked hard in the gospel but needed unity.

name: Syntyche
footnote: Called to agree in the Lord.

name: Clement
footnote: Fellow worker whose name is in the Book of Life.

name: Epaphroditus
footnote: Risked his life to serve Paul.

name: Onesiphorus
footnote: Refreshing and profitable servant.

name: Aristarchus
footnote: Loyal prisoner with Paul.

name: Zacchaeus
footnote: Tax collector made pure by Jesus.

name: Bartimaeus
footnote: Blind beggar healed and followed Jesus.

name: Jairus
footnote: Synagogue ruler whose daughter was raised.

name: Simeon (NT)
footnote: Held baby Jesus and declared he had “seen” salvation.

name: Anna
footnote: Prophetess who recognized the Messiah.

name: Elizabeth
footnote: Mother of John; God kept His oath.

name: Zacharias
footnote: Father of John; God remembered him.

name: John the Baptist
footnote: Prepared the way with grace.

name: Herodias
footnote: Manipulative “heroine” who sought John’s head.

name: Cleopas
footnote: Disciple on Emmaus road who saw the risen Christ.

name: Matthias
footnote: Chosen by lot to replace Judas.

name: Philip (evangelist)
footnote: Evangelized Samaria and the Ethiopian.

name: Simon the Sorcerer
footnote: Heard the gospel but sought power.

name: Dorcas (Tabitha)
footnote: Full of good works; raised to life.

name: Sergius Paulus
footnote: Proconsul who believed after seeing God’s power.

name: Elymas (Bar-Jesus)
footnote: Opposed the gospel.

name: Jason
footnote: Hosted Paul and faced riot.

name: Dionysius
footnote: Areopagite who believed Paul’s message.

name: Damaris
footnote: Athenian woman who joined the believers.

name: Gallio
footnote: Proconsul who dismissed charges against Paul.

name: Alexander the coppersmith
footnote: Opposed Paul.

name: Hymenaeus
footnote: False teacher who shipwrecked faith.

name: Phygelus
footnote: Deserted Paul in Asia.

name: Hermogenes
footnote: Also deserted.

name: Crescens
footnote: Faithful coworker who went to Galatia.

name: Pudens
footnote: Roman Christian who greeted Paul.

name: Linus
footnote: Early Church leader.

name: Claudia
footnote: Woman who greeted Paul.

name: Eubulus
footnote: Faithful in Rome.

name: Zenas
footnote: Lawyer who traveled with Apollos.

name: Jude (Judas, brother of James)
footnote: Author of the epistle of Jude.

name: Sosthenes
footnote: Ruler of synagogue who believed.

name: Crispus
footnote: Synagogue ruler baptized by Paul.

name: Fortunatus
footnote: Corinthian who refreshed Paul.

name: Achaicus
footnote: Helped Paul.

name: Stephanas
footnote: First converts in Achaia.

name: Chloe
footnote: Informed Paul of divisions.

name: Nymphas
footnote: Hosted a house church.
